mainText: This is Dose of Good for Friday, November 13. Here are 5 good news stories. First: Teenager lost in the bush for six days found alive in Australia. William, 17, went missing on his first solo camping trip. After a search involving hundreds of people, a police helicopter spotted him asleep in a dry riverbed. He is well and back with his mum. Second: Brazilian trial shows tighter blood pressure control prevents repeat strokes. The Optimal-Stroke trial followed 4,368 people for four years at 30 centres. Keeping systolic pressure under 120 cut new strokes from 6.4% to 4.7%. It was published in the New England Journal of Medicine. Third: Mangroves are growing back worldwide after decades of loss. Satellite images from 1984 to 2023 show that after losing 3,000 km² by 2010, mangroves have gained almost 2,000 km² since. A third came from restoration; Myanmar's have grown 10%. Fourth: Decoy crops trick a weed into killing itself as Australia nears eradication. To wipe out red witchweed, scientists plant soybeans that make its seeds sprout with no host to latch onto. The infested area shrank from 110 to 4.3 hectares in 11 years. Fifth: AI fine-tunes a brain implant that gives a blind man flashes of sight. A 27-year-old who lost his sight received a 96-electrode brain implant. AI picked more precise stimulation using less current. It's still experimental: he perceives flashes and shapes of light. That was your dose for today. See you tomorrow!
